summary: Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).
Hirotomo Teranishi succeeded Hiroshi Kanno in 2009 and served as director at Soka University (attested 2010–2011).

Hisao Inagaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (~1949–1955) and the University of London (~1966–1968). He held posts at SOAS University of London in 1970 and Ryukoku University as professor (~1981–2000).
Hisao Kanaseki was a scholar of Buddhist studies who studied at Doshisha University (~1937–1941) and held a post at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1966–1982).

Hisao Takahashi, an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Taisho University under Ryukai Mano. He held various posts at Taisho University, including professor (~1998–2015), and was a researcher at the Buzan-ha Institute of Modern Mission (attested 1995).

Hisashi Matsumura is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He held posts at the Australian National University (attested 1982) and Kobe Shinwa University as an assistant professor (attested 1996).

Hisashi Sato was a Tibetology and history scholar who studied at Kyoto University (~1934–1937). He taught Katsumi Mimaki and Tsuguhito Takeuchi, and held professorships at Kyoto University (~1964–1977), Toyo University (~1977–1984), Komazawa University, and a post at Bukkyo University.

Hisataka Ishida works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He earned his doctorate at the University of Vienna under Helmut Krasser, having also studied under Akira Saito, Hiroshi Marui, Yoichi Fukuda, and Masahiro Inami, and lectured at Aichi Gakuin University (attested 2015).
Hitoshi Inui is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Kanjin Horiuchi. He held posts at Koyasan University as a lecturer (attested 1986–1992) and later as a professor (attested 2015).

Hitoshi Katō works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and philosophy. Attested in 1992 at Osaka University of Foreign Studies, Nara University of Education, and Otani University, he later served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 2016–2017).
Hitoshi Obara is a scholar of history, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Hokkaido University (~1964–1968). He served as a professor at the University of the Sacred Heart (~1996–2015).

Hjalmar Edgren was a linguist and Indologist who studied at the University of Nebraska–Lincoln and under William Dwight Whitney (~1871–1874). He held posts at Lund University (~1880–1885), the University of Gothenburg (~1891–1893), and the University of Nebraska–Lincoln (~1885–1901).
Hla Pe was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Yangon (~1930–1935) and the University of London (~1938–1944). He taught Gustaaf Houtman.
Ho-chin Yang is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Washington under Leonard van der Kuijp (attested 1994).
Ho-sung Kim works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He founded the Institute for the History of Japanese Buddhism and served as a professor at Dongguk University (attested 2011).

Hojun Nagasaki studied at Nava Nalanda Mahavihara and specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. He held a position at Otani University (~1974–1999), became professor emeritus (~1999), and served as president of the Japanese Association for Jain Studies in 1998.

Holly Gayley is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. She completed doctoral studies at Harvard University (~2001–2009) and held a post at the University of Colorado Boulder (~2008).

Hong Luo is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology scholar who was a doctoral student at Peking University. He has held posts at the China Tibetology Research Center and as a professor at Sichuan University.
Honsho Ueda is a Buddhist studies scholar who served at Minobusan University as a lecturer (attested 1963) and later as a professor (attested 1992; 1996–2001).
Hoong Teik Toh is a scholar of sinology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD from Harvard University in 2004, studying under Gray Tuttle, Ruohong Li, Hongmei Jin, and Yudru Tsomu.
